Test steps: Run notideck --version.
Expected result: Returns 0.1.0.

Test steps: Run notideck serve.
Expected result: Server starts without errors.
Console loads successfully.

Test steps: Run notideck doctor.
Expected result: Reports a current database schema.

Test steps: Restart the server and inspect your records.
Expected result: Users, channels, sources, rules and history are preserved.

Test steps: Sign in with the exact username and password.
Expected result: Login succeeds; usernames are currently case-sensitive.

Test steps: Attempt login with an incorrect password.
Expected result: Login is rejected.

Test steps: Log out, then try to access protected data.
Expected result: Authentication is required again.

Test steps: Change your password; test the old and new passwords.
Expected result: New password works; old password fails; existing sessions are revoked.

Test steps: Sign in as a Viewer and attempt configuration changes.
Expected result: Operational data is readable; changes are denied.

Test steps: Sign in as an Operator; test channel/rule edits, retries, user management and queue clearing.
Expected result: Channel/rule edits and retries allowed; user management and queue clearing denied.

Test steps: Disable a separate test user and attempt login with that account.
Expected result: Disabled user cannot log in.

Test steps: Create and edit a test source.
Expected result: Saved values persist correctly.

Test steps: Create a source API key and copy it privately.
Expected result: Key appears once and is scoped to the source.

Test steps: Submit a notification using a valid source key.
Expected result: HTTP 202 and a notification ID are returned.

Test steps: Submit with no key, then with an incorrect key.
Expected result: Both requests are rejected.

Test steps: Revoke a test key and submit using it.
Expected result: Request is rejected.

Test steps: Disable a test source and submit using its key.
Expected result: New submission is rejected.

Test steps: Submit with a valid key but a different source name.
Expected result: Cross-source submission is rejected.

Test steps: Create a channel, edit it, save and reopen it.
Expected result: Configuration persists.

Test steps: Reopen a channel containing credentials.
Expected result: Stored secrets are masked.

Test steps: Use Test Channel for an enabled test destination.
Expected result: A real test message arrives; provider acceptance is reported.
Notes: Sends real notifications. Use non-sensitive messages and destinations you control.

Test steps: Test a separate channel with deliberately invalid settings.
Expected result: A useful failure diagnostic appears.

Test steps: Disable a test channel and submit an event targeting it.
Expected result: Channel does not dispatch notifications.

Test steps: Duplicate a test channel.
Expected result: Copy starts disabled.

Test steps: Test each additional provider you intend to use; list results in observations.
Expected result: Required providers deliver successfully; unused providers remain Not tested.
Actual result / observations: Verified providers: Email (SMTP) and Telegram only. WhatsApp, Signal, SMS (Twilio), Slack, Discord, and Generic HTTP Webhook remain not tested by the user.
Notes: Sends real notifications. Use non-sensitive messages and destinations you control.

Test steps: Submit an event matching source, environment and severity conditions.
Expected result: Selected destination receives a delivery job and message.

Test steps: Submit an event that matches no enabled rule.
Expected result: Event is stored as UNROUTED with no deliveries.

Test steps: For severity gte ERROR, submit WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL events.
Expected result: ERROR and CRITICAL match; WARNING does not.

Test steps: Route one event to multiple test channels.
Expected result: Each destination has its own tracked delivery.

Test steps: Make two rules target the same channel and recipient; submit one event.
Expected result: Only one delivery is created for that channel/recipient.

Test steps: Run simulation with a sample event.
Expected result: Expected destinations appear; nothing is sent.

Test steps: Change enabled state, priority or conditions; submit new events without restarting.
Expected result: New events use the updated rules.

Test steps: Open Templates.
Expected result: Audit, replication lag, connection failure, long-running query and backup status templates appear.

Test steps: Edit a routing rule and choose a Notification template by name.
Expected result: Selection saves and applies to new matching events.

Test steps: Submit examples/postgres_audit_event.json through a rule accepting WARNING.
Expected result: Audit alert renders and reaches the chosen destination.
Notes: Sends real notifications. Use non-sensitive messages and destinations you control.

Test steps: Inspect the delivered audit example.
Expected result: Node, source, timestamp, database, user, client and message are correct.

Test steps: Inspect notification level and database severity in the audit example.
Expected result: Level is WARNING while SEVERITY is ERROR.

Test steps: Submit a templated event with optional metadata omitted.
Expected result: Rendering succeeds with blank/fallback values.

Test steps: Edit a template and submit another matching event.
Expected result: New event reflects the edit; already queued content is unchanged.

Test steps: After SMTP relay access works, send a templated email.
Expected result: HTML formatting is readable and values display correctly.
Notes: Sends real notifications. Use non-sensitive messages and destinations you control. Resolve SMTP relay authorization first.

Test steps: Stop the worker and submit an event matching an enabled destination.
Expected result: Delivery stays queued.

Test steps: Start notideck worker with a queued event.
Expected result: Worker processes the event.

Test steps: Inspect a successful delivery.
Expected result: Attempt is recorded and delivery becomes SENT; SENT means provider acceptance, not a receipt.

Test steps: Pause dispatch, submit an event, then resume.
Expected result: New job waits while paused and dispatches after resume.

Test steps: Pause one of two test channels, submit events, then resume it.
Expected result: Only that channel waits; other channel continues.

Test steps: Generate a controlled failed delivery and open its history.
Expected result: Useful redacted error details appear.

Test steps: Correct a failed channel configuration and retry its failed delivery.
Expected result: New attempt occurs; previous attempt history is retained.

Test steps: Preview cancellation for pending test jobs.
Expected result: Affected count is shown before confirmation.

Test steps: Confirm cancellation of eligible pending jobs.
Expected result: Jobs become CANCELLED; notification history remains.

Test steps: Open a notification and its delivery timeline.
Expected result: Original event and individual attempts are visible.

Test steps: Filter by severity/environment and search notification titles.
Expected result: Results match the selected criteria.

Test steps: Create more than 20 test events and navigate pages.
Expected result: Records paginate correctly without missing or duplicated page entries.

Test steps: Compare dashboard/queue counts against test activity.
Expected result: Counts update to reflect persisted activity.

Test steps: Perform an administrative change and inspect Audit logs.
Expected result: Action appears with actor and timestamp.

Test steps: Use light/dark mode and your usual browser/window sizes.
Expected result: Controls remain readable and usable.

Test steps: Submit the same payload twice with the same idempotency_key.
Expected result: Same notification ID; no duplicate delivery jobs.

Test steps: Reuse the key with a different message.
Expected result: Request is rejected with a conflict.

Test steps: Submit with a new key.
Expected result: A new notification is created.

Test steps: Submit a correctly signed webhook and an invalid signature.
Expected result: Valid request succeeds; invalid signature is rejected.
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.

Test steps: Configure recipient addresses/group, route an event to the group.
Expected result: Matching recipient addresses receive independent deliveries.
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.

Test steps: In an isolated installation, complete setup, ingest, dispatch and restart using the intended database.
Expected result: Migration, delivery and persistence succeed.
Actual result / observations: Postgres checked, but tls/ssl should be check or unchacked
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.

Test steps: If required, repeat setup, ingestion, delivery and restart using a dedicated Oracle test database.
Expected result: Required flows work; record database and driver versions.
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.

Test steps: Build/start isolated web and worker containers; test delivery and restart with persistent volumes.
Expected result: Containers run and application data survives restart.
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.

Test steps: Test login, logout, API ingestion and sessions behind the intended HTTPS proxy.
Expected result: Authentication, secure cookies and same-origin operations work.
Notes: Optional: test if required for your deployment.
